svg.text: I — The round trip (§36.3 → §36.2)
The one sanctioned path from a plugin edit back to the spec. It drafts; it never merges — what reaches main is always a spec change with a plugin regenerated from it.
Start — a direct edit to claude-plugin/openaos/skills/*/SKILL.md, the drafting surface
Editing a SKILL.md is concrete and small; editing §12 of a large specification is not. Prototyping here is sanctioned, for maintainers and contributors alike.
§36.3 Spec Sync (Plugin → Spec)
Triggered by "Using the runbook, sync the design spec with the plugin." No precondition.
1 · Detect scope — two buckets
Mechanical — content/* and workflow-specs/*, by byte comparison.
Authored — skills/*/SKILL.md against spec §8.1, §12, §13.
Scope narrowed by sync-state.py status; where absent, the full comparison runs. No drift → stop.
2 · Tenet check — the gate
Every changed file in both buckets is checked against the five tenets in §33.1.
3 · Mechanical sync
Tenet-passing copies go plugin → design-spec verbatim (sync-plugin-to-spec.py --apply).
4 · Authored reflection
Draft the §8.1/§12/§13 update, preserving spec-only rationale and cross-references.
The draft is a starting point. You review it, edit it, and own the spec language that results.
5 · Combined preview
every spec file this would touch, both buckets, plus the exclusions
6 · Proceed gate
one gate for the whole batch — write only on the exact word
7 · Validate and re-baseline
Re-run the six validators, then python scripts/sync-state.py record.
8 · Revision history
"Spec sync from plugin: [files]." No automatic version bump — §36.3 restores equality.
9 · Close the round trip
Direct the user to §36.2 to regenerate the plugin from the now-updated spec.
The five fundamental design tenets (§33.1)
Drawn from what is already normative — not newly invented.
1 · Scope discipline
exactly three things; nothing the Frame removed may come back
2 · Governance layer is not removable
the Proceed gate, governance.md, the router, the five workflows
3 · Skills vs. workflows boundary
skills are plugin-owned; workflows are user-owned and refinable
4 · Drift invariant
definition files change only through sanctioned, gated paths
5 · Single-artifact distribution
one plugin, one openaos_version, one spec — no new artifact types
Tenet 3 resists mechanical checking: any change touching the
refinability boundary surfaces for human review regardless.
Fails a tenet → not reflected
The file is excluded from this sync and reported by name and by the
tenet it violated. Nothing is ever silently dropped.
Appended to design-spec/sync-exclusions.md with disposition open.
An open entry is a finding on the next §36.1 issue list (§34), which
gates finalization. It clears by recording any disposition —
including an explicit decision not to act.
Passes → steps 3 and 4
Mechanical files are copied verbatim; skill changes become a spec draft
for the author to review and own.
The spec is the source of truth again at the next commit boundary.
Ordering rule (§33) — §36.3 always runs before §36.2 in any cycle. The two directions are never concurrently live, so there is no conflict resolution to write.
What actually reaches main — and what CI checks
· CI asserts byte-identity on every pull request: validate-content.py (VC1–VC13), validate-workflow-specs.py (WS1–WS2), and the skill anchors (SK1–SK5).
· The tenet check is deliberately not in CI — it is a judgment call, not a script. CI enforces the byte-identity invariant instead.
· §36.3 is a drafting aid, not a second route to main. What you submit is a spec change, with the plugin regenerated from it.
Sync state (.openaos-sync-state.json) is local, gitignored, and recomputable — it records both hashes per file pair, so divergence on either side breaks the match.
